summary.short: Peru's 2013 Cybercrime Law (Ley 30096) criminalises offences against computer systems and data, computer fraud, identity theft, illicit data trafficking, interception, and child-related offences committed via ICT. It also requires telecom concessionaires and other companies to provide data or geolocation under judicial orders.
summary.long: Law 30096, published 22 October 2013, criminalises computer-related offences and sets prison terms and day-fines. Arts. 2-4 cover unlawful access and data and system integrity. Art. 5 penalises contact with minors for sexual purposes via ICT. Art. 6 covers illegal data trafficking and Art. 7 interception of non-public data transmissions, with heavier terms for classified information or national defence and security. Art. 8 covers computer fraud, Art. 9 identity theft and Art. 10 making or distributing devices, programmes or passwords designed for these offences. Art. 11 allows sentences to be raised by up to one third for criminal-organisation membership, abuse of access positions, economic gain, or harm to social aid, defence or security. Final provisions authorise undercover agents, order police-prosecutor protocols, and direct the banking and telecom regulators to set fine scales for supervised firms that fail to meet judicial information orders. Amendments to the Criminal Procedure Code require telecom concessionaires to provide geolocation and call data within 30 working days and keep equipment compatible with the police interception system; cybercrime is added to wiretap and organised-crime lists, and Penal Code provisions on telephone interference, child pornography and discrimination are amended.

notes: The text contains erratum notes (Fe de erratas, 23 Oct 2013) for the amendments to Ley 27697 and the Código Procesal Penal. The repeal provision carries a marker '(*) RECTIFICADO POR FE DE ERRATAS' without the erratum text. The Código Penal (DL 635) and Código Procesal Penal (DL 957) are not reproduced in full; amendments restate only the affected articles. Art. 7 paragraphs 2 and 3 (classified information, national defence) repeat wording now also inserted into Art. 162 of the Código Penal by the Cuarta amendment. Relations stated only in other instruments (e.g., DL 991 and Ley 30077 amending Ley 27697) are not coded here.

enforcement.max_penalty_text: Base: prison term not less than 6 nor more than 10 years and 120 to 365 días multa. Aggravated (minor under 14, or material disseminated through ICT): not less than 10 nor more than 12 years and 50 to 365 días multa
enforcement.penalty_formula: Prison term 6 to 10 years plus 120 to 365 días multa (base); 10 to 12 years plus 50 to 365 días multa (aggravated); further tier 12 to 15 years for specified cases
enforcement.penalty_reference: Código Penal Art. 183-A (as modified by Ley 30096, Disp. Compl. Modif. Cuarta)

evidence.provision: Disposición Complementaria Modificatoria Cuarta (Código Penal, Art. 183-A)
evidence.quote: no menor de seis ni mayor de diez años y con ciento

enforcement.authority: Not specified in the provision; criminal courts
enforcement.triggered_by: Discrimination on listed grounds (Penal Code Art. 323, as restated in Disposición Complementaria Modificatoria Cuarta); aggravated for public officials; same penalty where discrimination is carried out through ICT
enforcement.max_penalty_text: Base: prison term not less than 2 nor more than 3 years or community service of 60 to 120 jornadas. Public official or servant: not less than 2 nor more than 4 years and disqualification under Art. 36 numeral 2. Discrimination through ICT: same penalty as the base tier
enforcement.penalty_formula: Prison term 2 to 3 years or 60 to 120 jornadas of community service (base); 2 to 4 years plus disqualification (public official)
enforcement.penalty_reference: Código Penal Art. 323 (as modified by Ley 30096, Disp. Compl. Modif. Cuarta)
